slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Latex particles coated with goat IgG anti-human CRP agglutinate when mixed with samples containing CRP (qualitative and semi-quantitative slide test).
CRP is an acute-phase protein that rises sharply after tissue injury, bacterial and viral infection, inflammation and malignancy; it can reach 300 mg/L within 12–24 hours.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “CRP-Latex” kit (IFU SGIS03-I, 17/01/23). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: fresh serum — stable 7 days at 2–8 °C or 3 months at −20 °C. Centrifuge samples containing fibrin; do not use highly haemolysed or lipaemic samples.
Latex reagent (pH 8.2); positive control (red cap) — human serum with CRP > 20 mg/L; negative control (blue cap) — animal serum.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: mechanical rotator adjustable to 80–100 r.p.m., vortex mixer, 50 µL pipettes, disposable slides (in the kit), stirrers.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (latex test)
bullets: All components are ready to use and stable until expiry when stored tightly closed at 2–8 °C.
Do not freeze: frozen reagents could change the functionality of the test.
Mix the reagents gently before use; bring reagents and samples to room temperature (sensitivity falls at low temperatures).
Signs of deterioration: particles and turbidity.
This test is read by eye on a slide — no semi-automatic photometric analyser programme is needed. Values come from the SPINREACT “CRP-Latex” IFU (SGIS03-I); your own kit IFU takes precedence.

slides.title: Procedure: qualitative method
bullets: 1. Bring the reagents and samples to room temperature.
2. Place 50 µL of the sample and one drop each of the positive and negative controls into separate circles on the slide.
3. Mix the CRP-latex reagent vigorously (or on a vortex) and add one drop (50 µL) next to each sample.
4. Mix the drops with a stirrer, spreading them over the whole circle; use a new stirrer for each sample.

slides.title: Procedure: qualitative method
bullets: 5. Rotate the slide on a mechanical rotator at 80–100 r.p.m. for 2 minutes.
6. Read immediately after removing from the rotator: reading later than 2 minutes can give false positives.

slides.title: Reading and calculation
rows: Make serial two-fold dilutions of the sample in 9 g/L saline; test each dilution as in the qualitative method.
The highest dilution showing a positive result

slides.title: Reading and calculation
rows: up to 6 mg/L; each laboratory sets its own range

slides.title: Errors, interferences and limitations
bullets: The strength of agglutination does not indicate the concentration.
Analytical sensitivity 6 (5–10) mg/L. No prozone effect up to 1600 mg/L.
Very high CRP may give a negative result (prozone) — re-test using a 20 µL drop of the sample.
Bilirubin (20 mg/dL), haemoglobin (10 g/L) and lipids (10 g/L) do not interfere; rheumatoid factors (100 IU/mL) do.

slides.title: Errors, interferences and limitations
bullets: Clinical diagnosis should not rest on a single test result; integrate clinical and laboratory data.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Run the positive and negative controls with the patient samples in every series — they also serve as a comparison pattern.
IFU: any result different from the negative control is considered positive.
If the controls do not give the expected result, do not release patient results; check the reagent and technique.
Sensitivity is calibrated to the reference material ERM-DA 474/IFCC.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Latex reagent: H360 — may damage fertility or the unborn child.
Controls (+/−): H317 — may cause an allergic skin reaction (contain a preservative).
Components of human origin tested negative for HBsAg, HCV and antibody to HIV (1/2); still handle them as potentially infectious.
Serum is potentially infectious: wear gloves, never pipette by mouth; disinfect used slides and stirrers.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
